title: Change the scooter final gear oil
summary: Swap the small amount of gear oil in a scooter's rear hub. Cheap, quick and often forgotten.
tools: Socket for the drain and filler bolts
Syringe or squeeze bottle with a hose
parts: Gear oil (grade and amount on your spec sheet)
New crush washers for both bolts

steps.text: Ride for a few minutes to warm the oil, then park on the center stand on level ground.
Find the two bolts on the rear hub: the filler bolt sits higher, the drain bolt at the bottom. Remove the filler bolt first.
steps.caution: Loosen the filler first. If the drain comes out and the filler is seized, you can't refill and the bike is stuck.

steps.text: Remove the drain bolt and let the oil drain completely.
Fit a new crush washer to the drain bolt and tighten it to the torque on your spec sheet.
Measure the exact amount from your spec sheet and inject it through the filler hole with the syringe or bottle.
steps.caution: Scooter hubs only hold about 100 to 150 mL. Overfilling pushes oil past the seal and onto the rear brake.

steps.text: Fit a new washer to the filler bolt, tighten it to spec and wipe the hub clean.
Ride a short distance, then check both bolts for leaks.
